subject.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]

question: Should backup excludes support automatic state-dir `.backupignore` loading and warning-only external-asset bypasses, or must the first core implementation require explicit opt-in and apply consistently to every archived asset?
rationale: This is a user-facing backup/security contract, not only a code-style choice: it controls whether existing state files can change backup contents without a flag and whether explicit excludes apply to external workspaces/config paths.

options.title: Require explicit, consistent excludes
options.body: Make `.backupignore` opt-in or clearly maintainer-approved, apply filters per asset root, and preserve current main backup safeguards before considering merge.

options.title: Accept current semantics deliberately
options.body: Document that automatic `.backupignore` and external-asset warning behavior are intentional, then require upgrade/security proof before merge.

options.title: Close or split the branch
options.body: Close this stale conflicting branch and keep the canonical feature issue open for a smaller replacement that starts from current backup code.

recommendation.title: Require explicit, consistent excludes
recommendation.body: Make `.backupignore` opt-in or clearly maintainer-approved, apply filters per asset root, and preserve current main backup safeguards before considering merge.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc most recently touched the current backup implementation on main and is best positioned to judge how this feature should fit the current backup pipeline.
